name: AnchorRIDES
operator: Municipality of Anchorage Public Transportation Department (operated by MV Transportation)
fare: $3.50 core ADA one-way (below $4.00 ADA max); cash exact fare or pre-paid ticket
hours: Comparable to People Mover fixed-route service hours/area
notes: Shared-ride, accessible door-to-door/curb-to-curb service for ADA-eligible persons with disabilities and seniors 60+; demand and subscription (recurring) trips; core and premium service levels; reservations day-before up to 7 days in advance. ADA paratransit is highest service priority; seniors may face denials at capacity/funding limits.

name: CAPITAL AKcess (formerly Care-A-Van)
area: City and Borough of Juneau, AK
operator: Capital Transit (City and Borough of Juneau); contract operator Ground Transportation Solutions (since Nov 1, 2025)
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for individuals whose disabling conditions prevent fixed-route use; ADA eligibility certification required. Reservations day-before, up to ~2 weeks (14 days) in advance. Renamed from Care-A-Van in Feb 2020. Contract operator changed to Ground Transportation Solutions effective Nov 1, 2025.

name: Valley Transit Demand Response
area: Matanuska-Susitna (Mat-Su) Borough, AK — zoned areas of the Valley (Wasilla, Palmer, Houston, Big Lake, Meadow Lakes, Knik-Goose Bay, Fairview, Port MacKenzie, Butte)
fare: $3 general public per zone traveled; $2 seniors 60+ and youth 17 & under per zone
notes: Point-to-point zoned curb-to-curb demand-response open to the general public; bookable up to ~2 weeks in advance; reported ~24,700 riders/year with daily waitlists.

name: Van Tran
area: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Fairbanks / North Pole), AK — within ¾ mile of MACS fixed routes
hours: Mon–Fri 6:00 AM–9:45 PM, Sat 8:45 AM–7:45 PM, closed Sun
notes: Borough's ADA complementary demand-response service for people whose physical, cognitive, or sensory disabilities prevent use of MACS fixed-route buses; eligibility via application, medical documentation, and in-person assessment. Trips reservable same-day up to two weeks in advance; service prioritized by proximity (¾-mile) to fixed routes.

name: BRATS On-Demand
area: Baldwin County, AL (countywide; Eastern Shore, Foley, Robertsdale, Bay Minette, Gulf Shores areas)
operator: Baldwin County Commission - Baldwin Regional Area Transit System (BRATS)
fare: Distance-based (each way): 0-5 mi $2.00, 6-10 mi $2.50, 11-15 mi $3.00, +$0.50 per additional 5 mi
notes: Public door-to-door shared-ride on-demand service. Same-area trips available ASAP; can book up to 7 days in advance (per official site). Launched Sept 2020 via FTA Integrated Mobility Innovation (IMI) grant originally with Via; now operates on Spare platform. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles available on request.

name: ClasTran
area: Jefferson, Shelby, and Walker counties, AL (Birmingham region)
fare: Subsidized $4 one-way / $8 round trip (unsubsidized higher rates outside BJCTA area)
notes: Curb-to-curb demand-response for persons 60+, persons with disabilities, and rural-area residents; reserve at least one day in advance (next-day reservations before 11am). Nonprofit consortium founded 1995, service began 1997; subsidized by local governments plus federal matching funds via the MPO.

name: MAX On-Demand (formerly Birmingham On-Demand)
area: Birmingham & Jefferson County, AL microtransit zones: Downtown/City Center, East/Airport, North Birmingham, Mountain Brook, Homewood (Irondale pilot); ~26.6 sq mi core coverage
operator: Birmingham Jefferson County Transit Authority (MAX Transit); previously City of Birmingham; powered by Via
fare: $1.50 flat per shared ride; $0.75 per additional passenger
hours: Varies by zone (e.g. Downtown Mon-Fri 6am-7pm, Sat 10am-6pm; East/Airport Mon-Sat 5am-9pm)
funding: Local (City of Birmingham), Federal (FTA); Greater Birmingham Community Foundation grants for Homewood/Irondale pilots
fleet: Not specified (Via-branded vans; wheelchair-accessible vehicles available)
notes: Corner-to-corner shared microtransit launched 2019 under City of Birmingham/Via; Sept 2025 City Council transferred the program and $2.5M in funding to BJCTA/MAX Transit and rebranded it MAX On-Demand; expanded into suburban zones (Mountain Brook, North Birmingham) and July 2026 15-month pilots in Homewood ($792K) and Irondale ($513.75K). Max trip ~3.5 miles.

name: MoGo Rideshare
area: 17-mile service zone, City of Mobile, AL (workforce/employment corridors)
operator: Mobile Area Chamber of Commerce Foundation, operated by Via
fare: Free to employment/training centers (AIDT, Airbus, Austal USA, FlightPath9); $1.25 to other destinations
funding: Federal (Carbon Reduction Program via South Alabama Regional Planning Commission), Local (City of Mobile), Community Foundation of South Alabama, Alabama Power Foundation, Blue Cross Blue Shield Caring Foundation
notes: Launched March 16, 2024 as workforce-access pilot; corner-to-corner shared rides with virtual stops; received over $500,000 in Carbon Reduction Program grants. Being incorporated into a redesigned Via-led Mobile transit network launching July 2026.

name: The M: Micro Transit
area: City of Montgomery, AL — mapped zones incl. Downtown Montgomery, Montgomery Regional Airport, Montgomery Whitewater, Maxwell AFB Visitor Center, Jackson Hospital
fare: $1.50 per ride (promotional; credit/debit or exact cash to driver)
notes: On-demand shared rideshare; requests booked in real time with short wait times, or scheduled up to 7 days in advance; open to general public; complements fixed-route bus.

name: Tuscaloosa Transit Demand Response
operator: Tuscaloosa Transit Authority (Tuscaloosa County Parking and Transit Authority)
fare: $2.00 per boarding; personal care attendant rides free
notes: Eligibility restricted to individuals within city limits with physical and/or mental disabilities; door-to-door service to appointments, dialysis, shopping, etc.; personal care attendants ride free.

name: GOJO Paratransit (formerly JET Paratransit)
area: City of Jonesboro, Arkansas (ADA complementary paratransit within 3/4 mile of fixed routes)
operator: City of Jonesboro (GOJO / Jonesboro Economical Transportation)
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for riders with a functional mobility limitation preventing use of fixed-route buses; part of Jonesboro's GOJO system (formerly JET), which rebranded in March 2026 marking the system's 20th anniversary. Contact 870-935-5387.

name: METRO Connect
area: Central Arkansas zones: John Barrow Road, Riverdale, Levy-Amboy, East Little Rock, Hensley (Little Rock); North Little Rock; Sherwood; Conway
operator: Rock Region METRO (Central Arkansas Transit Authority)
fare: Standard METRO fares (cash, passes, Token Transit; Conway zone exact cash or virtual 1-Ride passes only)
notes: On-demand, point-to-point-within-zone shared microtransit connecting to fixed-route transfers; started 2020 with a John Barrow test zone, since expanded to eight zones; migrated from TransLoc to Via platform; walk-up bookings eliminated Oct 2023; Conway public zone launched Oct 2024.

name: ORT On-Demand
area: Northwest Arkansas city zones: Fayetteville, Springdale, Rogers (Mon-Sat); Bentonville (Sat only)
fare: $1.25 per trip for up to 5 riders in a group
notes: App-based on-demand shared rides (door-to-door) within defined zones around NWA cities; may direct riders to fixed routes when faster. Program began in Rogers ~2020 and expanded to Bentonville/Fayetteville Feb 2022 (2 buses each in Rogers/Bentonville at that time); ride requests grew from ~500/week (Feb 2022) to ~1,500/week (Jul 2022).

name: DART Connect
area: Three on-demand zones: Georgetown and Millsboro (Sussex County) and Newark (New Castle County), DE
operator: Delaware Transit Corporation (DART First State), a division of DelDOT
booking: App (DART Transit / DART Connect app), Phone (1-800-652-DART, Option 3)
fare: $2.00 per ride (same as DART bus fare); day/week/30-day/20-ride passes available
hours: Newark: Mon-Fri 6am-8pm; Georgetown & Millsboro: Mon-Fri 5:45am-8pm; no service on DART holidays
fleet: Minibuses / mini-transit buses (~11 seats each; Newark launched with two vehicles)
notes: State's first on-demand microtransit. Georgetown/Millsboro launched Apr 12, 2021 as an FTA-funded pilot replacing Flex Routes 901/902; continued after pilot success. Newark added Aug 2023, replacing the Unicity fixed-route loop. Waits estimated no more than 15 min. Available to the general public; first/last-mile connections to regular DART routes.

name: DART First State Paratransit
area: Statewide DE; ADA trips within 3/4 mile of DART fixed routes across New Castle, Kent, and Sussex counties, plus non-ADA demand-response areas
operator: Delaware Transit Corporation (DART First State), a division of DelDOT
fare: $4.00 ADA paratransit or connector trip; $6.00 non-ADA demand-response trip
hours: Matches local fixed-route days/hours for ADA trips
notes: Eligibility-restricted service for people with disabilities (three ADA categories) plus an elderly-only program for riders 65+. ADA trips are within 3/4 mile of a fixed route during its operating hours; non-ADA trips are demand-response. Requires certified eligibility application with healthcare-professional verification (Part A/Part B); temporary eligibility granted pending determination (within 21 days). Reservations required at least one day in advance.

name: Hele-On Ka Hoʻokele (Rural Door-to-Door Service)
area: Rural areas outside Hele-On fixed routes: Seaview/Kalapana, Upper Puna, Waimea, Hilo, Kailua-Kona, Captain Cook; Island of Hawaiʻi
operator: Hawaiʻi County Economic Opportunity Council (HCEOC), operating for the County of Hawaiʻi Mass Transit Agency
hours: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM, excluding County-observed holidays
funding: Local (County of Hawaiʻi Mass Transit Agency)
notes: Open to the general public who reside in rural areas outside regular fixed-route and paratransit coverage. Registration required; reservations at (808) 731-7009 option 3, minimum one day in advance, up to 14 days ahead. Riders travel within a district or are taken to the nearest Hele-On fixed-route stop for onward travel.

name: Hele-On Kākoʻo Paratransit
area: Island of Hawaiʻi — Hilo, Puna, and Kailua-Kona service areas (within 3/4 mile of fixed-route stops); Hawaiʻi County
operator: MTM Transit under contract to County of Hawaiʻi Mass Transit Agency
fare: Free (all Hele-On services fare-free through Dec 31, 2028)
hours: Hilo Mon-Sat 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m., Sun 9:15 a.m.-6:00 p.m.; Kailua-Kona daily 6:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m.; Puna Mon-Fri 5:30 a.m.-10:05 p.m., Sat/Sun 6:30 a.m.-9:15 p.m.
fleet: Not specified (MTM local staff of 13; offices in Hilo and Kailua-Kona; parent Hele-On fleet 30+ buses/vans/trolley)
notes: ADA complementary origin-to-destination paratransit for riders unable to use fixed-route Hele-On. MTM Transit contract went live Jan 1, 2023. Rides booked via the Via-built 'Hele-On Kakoʻo Paratransit' app (iOS/Android) or reservation line 808-640-1020 (island-wide daily 7:45 a.m.-4:30 p.m.); advance/next-day reservations. Eligibility functional, not diagnosis/age/income based.

name: Maui Bus ADA Paratransit Service
area: Corridors extending 3/4-mile on each side of fixed Maui Bus routes (central, south, west, Haʻiku, Kula, Upcountry), Maui County, HI
operator: Maui Economic Opportunity, Inc. (MEO Transportation) for the County of Maui Department of Transportation
fare: $2.00 one-way; 12-ride ticket book $20.00; PCA and service animal ride free
hours: Same as fixed-route Maui Bus (approx. 5:30 AM–10:00 PM depending on location, daily incl. holidays); reservation line 8:00 AM–4:00 PM daily
funding: Federal, Local (County of Maui; ADA complementary paratransit)
notes: Advance-reservation, curb-to-curb ADA paratransit for those unable to use fixed-route Maui Bus. Reservations (808) 877-7651; up to 14 days in advance, at least one day prior by 4:00 PM for next-day service. MEO awarded a 5-year County contract in 2023.

name: Seniors and Persons with Disabilities Demand Response Transportation (Hele-On / Hawaiʻi County)
operator: Hawaii County Economic Opportunity Council (HCEOC), under contract to the County of Hawaiʻi Mass Transit Agency
funding: Local (County of Hawaiʻi Mass Transit Agency)
notes: Eligibility-restricted demand-response for seniors age 60+ and persons with disabilities; contracted to HCEOC by the County of Hawaiʻi Mass Transit Agency. Provides access to medical facilities, rehabilitation centers, nutrition sites, shopping, banks, post offices, government buildings and employment. Distinct from Hele-On Ka Hoʻokele (general-public rural door-to-door) and Hele-On Kakoʻo ADA paratransit (operated by MTM Transit). Contact HCEOC Transportation Division 808-731-7009.

name: The Kauaʻi Bus Paratransit Service
area: Island of Kauaʻi (Kauaʻi County), HI — corridor served by fixed routes from Hanalei to Kekaha, hub at Līhuʻe
fare: Differing fares by category (ADA, senior, adult, youth); seniors with Kupuna Care and Personal Care Attendants ride free
notes: Shared-ride, curb-to-curb origin-to-destination service for registered seniors (65+; 10 trips/month, with work and dialysis exemptions), Kupuna Care Transportation seniors, and ADA-certified riders. Reservations required no later than 4:30 PM the day prior.

name: TheHandi-Van
area: Island of Oʻahu (islandwide), City & County of Honolulu, HI
operator: Oahu Transit Services, Inc. (OTS) for the City & County of Honolulu Dept. of Transportation Services
fare: $2.50 per one-way trip effective 7/1/2026 (was $2.25); $2.00 low-income; no charge for PCA or service animal; paid via TheHandi-Van HOLO Card
hours: Islandwide; 24-hour service available within 3/4 mile of TheBus Routes 2 and 40
funding: Federal, Local (City & County of Honolulu; ADA complementary paratransit)
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for riders unable to independently use TheBus; curb-to-curb shared ride. Reserve 1 to 3 days ahead; reservations (808) 456-5555; eligibility (808) 538-0033.

name: DART Bus Plus (Paratransit)
area: Des Moines metro DART member cities (Base and Premium Service Zones): Altoona, Ankeny, Bondurant, Clive, Des Moines, Johnston, Urbandale, West Des Moines, Windsor Heights, and unincorporated Polk County
operator: Des Moines Area Regional Transit Authority (DART)
booking: Phone (515-283-8136); reservations accepted up to 7 days ahead (Base Zone), until 5 p.m. weekdays / 4 p.m. weekends the day before
fare: $3.50 per trip in Base Service Zone; $30 per trip in Premium Service Zone (Premium trips are non-Medicaid only)
hours: Comparable to DART fixed route: approx. Mon-Fri 5 a.m.-11 p.m., Sat 6 a.m.-10 p.m., Sun 7 a.m.-7 p.m.; reservation line Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-5 p.m.
notes: ADA door-to-door complementary paratransit; riders must apply and be certified via a DART Bus Service Eligibility Form with medical/qualified-professional verification (results within 21 days). Premium Service Zone (added Nov 2023) extends coverage to full member-community boundaries. Approved riders also ride DART fixed route free.

name: DART On Demand
area: Des Moines metro — Ankeny microtransit zone (active); Clive, Urbandale and Altoona zones planned fall 2026 under Reimagine DART
operator: Des Moines Area Regional Transit Authority (DART)
fare: $3.50 standard; $0.75 half-fare and children ages 6-10; pay via DART On Demand app, myDART app, DART pass/tokens, or exact change
hours: Ankeny zone: Monday–Friday 6:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m. (last trip booking 6:15 p.m.)
notes: Point-to-point on-demand shared rides within a defined zone using smaller buses; trips can be booked in real-time or scheduled in advance and may be shared. Ankeny zone runs as-is until Sept 28, 2026, then reconfigured Ankeny plus new Clive-Urbandale and Altoona zones launch fall 2026 under Reimagine DART. Ankeny zone bounds: NE 62nd Ave (south), SE Four Mile Dr (east), 36th St (north), SW Irvinedale Dr (west).

name: Dial-A-Ride (ADA Paratransit)
area: City of Ames (and within 3/4 mile of CyRide fixed routes)
operator: CyRide (operated under contract by Heart of Iowa Regional Transit Agency / HIRTA)
fare: $2 per ride; Personal Care Attendant rides free, companion pays same fare
hours: Operates during all hours CyRide fixed routes are running
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for riders unable to use fixed-route buses due to a disability; requires application/eligibility approval (up to 21 days). Door-to-door service booked by phone through HIRTA (1-877-686-0029); same-day trips accepted if time and space allow, otherwise scheduled in advance. Wheelchair lift-equipped service available.

name: EASE (East Ames Service Extension)
area: East Ames on-demand zone, Ames, IA (pickups within EASE zone plus Ames City Hall)
operator: CyRide (City of Ames / Iowa State University transit)
fare: $1.00 per trip (same as regular CyRide bus fare)
notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand service; riders use the Ride Pingo app or call CyRide (515-239-5600, at least 30 min ahead for call-ins). Pingo platform launched with CyRide Dec 2022 — The Routing Company's first Midwest on-demand agency partnership. Two-year TRC contract awarded Oct 2022; agency reported improved efficiency, reduced call-center volume, high rider satisfaction. Transfers to fixed routes at City Hall.

name: HIRTA On-Demand
area: Boone, Dallas, Jasper, Madison, Marion, Story and Warren counties (central Iowa)
operator: Heart of Iowa Regional Transit Agency (HIRTA)
hours: Mon-Fri 7:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. (Story County from 6:30 a.m.)
fleet: ADA-accessible / wheelchair-lift-equipped vehicles (fleet size not specified)
notes: General public, any trip purpose; same-day or advance booking; pickups within a 20-minute window, door-to-door across seven counties. HIRTA is an FTA ITS4US complete-trip deployment site.

name: LIFTS (Linn County Paratransit)
area: Cedar Rapids, Marion, and Hiawatha metro plus rural Linn County communities (Alburnett, Center Point, Central City, Coggon, Ely, Fairfax, Lisbon, Mount Vernon, Palo, Robins, Springville, Walker, etc.), Iowa
operator: Linn County, Iowa (Linn County Community Services / LIFTS)
fare: $3.00 one-way for seniors/persons with disabilities; $6.00 one-way general public (rural only); personal care attendant free
hours: Weekdays 5:15 a.m.-8 p.m. (metro) / 7 a.m.-5 p.m. (rural); Saturday 8 a.m.-5 p.m. (metro only); no Sunday service
notes: Door-to-door demand-response paratransit; metro service restricted to ADA-eligible seniors and persons with disabilities (eligibility administered via Cedar Rapids Transit), rural communities open to general public. Reservations by phone (319-892-5170) up to 7-30 days in advance, at least one day prior. Distinct from Cedar Rapids Transit's own ADA paratransit.

name: MET ParaTransit
area: Waterloo and Cedar Falls (Black Hawk County), Iowa
operator: Metropolitan Transit Authority of Black Hawk County (MET Transit)
fare: $3.00 one-way (sheet of ten tickets $30.00; PCA rides free)
hours: Mon-Fri 5:45 AM-6:45 PM; Sat 6:45 AM-5:45 PM
notes: Door-to-door service for people whose disability prevents use of MET fixed-route buses; complementary ADA paratransit. Reservations required 1 to 14 days in advance by phone at (319) 234-5714.

name: MuscaBus ParaTransit
fare: $2.00 per ride (sheet of 12 tickets $24.00; personal care attendants ride free)
notes: Eligibility-restricted paratransit for individuals unable to access the fixed route bus due to disability; day-ahead phone reservation required (call 263-8152); complements MuscaBus fixed colored routes. Candidate's 'open to the general public / not eligibility-restricted' claim is contradicted by the official ParaTransit page, which limits it to riders unable to use fixed routes due to disability.

name: Peoplerides
area: Hardin, Marshall, Poweshiek and Tama counties, Iowa
fare: In-town $2-$15 depending on county/city; out-of-town demand-response $2.89 per mile
notes: Established 1974; open to the general public including persons with disabilities; provides 50,000+ rides annually across the four counties using 20 ADA-accessible vehicles; offers both route and demand-response trips. Advance booking (at least one day) receives priority; same-day depends on driver availability. Medicaid-funded trips booked via broker (MTM); Marshalltown paratransit requires prior approval.

name: Region 8 Regional Transit Authority (RTA) On-Demand
area: Delaware, Dubuque (excl. City of Dubuque) and Jackson counties, northeast Iowa (Planning Area 8)
fleet: ~30 light-duty buses and accessible minivans; transitioning to 9-passenger vans
notes: Modernized rural demand-response using QRyde booking/routing/scheduling platform; ~100,000 passenger trips annually serving ~2,500 individuals. Advance reservations typically requested 24h ahead; same-day available subject to availability; ~10-min-out arrival notifications. Open to the general public; all vehicles wheelchair accessible.

name: River Bend Transit
area: Cedar, Clinton, Muscatine and Scott counties (Iowa Quad Cities region)
fare: Not specified (varies by county/contract; per-county fare cards; same-day trips at premium; veterans ride free)
hours: Varies by service; Bettendorf Dial-A-Bus Mon-Fri 6 a.m.-6 p.m., Sat 8:45 a.m.-5:40 p.m.
notes: Iowa's first regional consolidated transit system (est. 1978); general-public door-to-door demand-response serving seniors, people with disabilities, and the general public across the Iowa Quad Cities; also offers same-day service (premium fare), county services, low-income employment transportation, and contracted city services (e.g. Bettendorf Dial-A-Bus). FTA transit agency profile ID 70049.

name: SEIBUS (Southeast Iowa Bus)
area: Des Moines, Henry, Lee and Louisa counties, southeast Iowa
fare: $3.00 in-town one-way; $15–$30 medical shuttle; monthly passes offered by county (per Iowa DOT / SEIBUS)
hours: Monday–Friday, 6:00 AM–4:00 PM (county availability windows ~9:00 AM–3:00 PM)
fleet: Wheelchair-lift-equipped buses; fleet size not specified
notes: On-demand curb-to-curb demand-response with no fixed routes; open to the general public including persons with disabilities; advance booking required — appointments must be made no later than 2:00 PM the day prior to departure (no same-day). Iowa DOT classifies it as Demand-Response, Subscription. Ridership figures not found.

name: SWITA (Southwest Iowa Transit Agency)
area: Cass, Fremont, Harrison, Mills, Montgomery, Page, Pottawattamie and Shelby counties, SW Iowa
hours: Mon-Fri 6:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. (vehicles operate 24/7 pending availability)
notes: Public on-demand rideshare open to all residents of eight SW Iowa counties; also offers student, medical, work-route, taxi and excursion services. On-demand rides 6a-5p weekdays.

name: Sioux City Transit ADA Paratransit
area: City of Sioux City, IA (within city limits; ADA complementary to fixed route)
operator: Sioux City Transit System (reservations handled by Siouxland Regional Transit System / SRTS)
fare: $3.60 per one-way trip (twice the fixed-route adult fare) per City of Sioux City; SRTS brochure lists $4.00 curb-to-curb / $7.00 door-to-door
notes: Origin-to-destination accessible service for individuals unable to use fixed-route transit due to functional ability (ADA complementary paratransit). Reservations must be made the day prior to the trip via SRTS (712) 279-6919. Fare figure differs between City site ($3.60) and SRTS brochure ($4.00/$7.00).

name: Siouxland Regional Transit System (SRTS)
area: Cherokee, Ida, Monona, Plymouth and Woodbury counties (IA); southern Union County, SD; Dakota County, NE
hours: Mon-Sat 5:30 a.m.-7:00 p.m.; closed major holidays
fleet: ADA-accessible buses (seat belts); fleet size not specified
notes: Demand-responsive, ADA-accessible public transit open to the general public; curb-to-curb and door-to-door service; reservations requested ~24 hours in advance by phone.

name: The Jule MiniBus (ADA Paratransit)
area: City of Dubuque and East Dubuque, IA
notes: ADA complementary / senior (65+) eligibility-restricted door-to-door paratransit operated alongside The Jule's fixed routes. Trips must be scheduled at least 1 day and up to 14 days in advance. Dispatch: 563-690-6464. Personal care attendant rides free.

name: Trip Connect (Johnson County)
area: Iowa City, Coralville, University Heights, North Liberty, Tiffin, and all parts of Johnson County north of I-80 (evening service)
operator: Horizons NTS (Neighborhood Transportation Service), contracted by Johnson County Social Services
funding: Local (Johnson County, City of North Liberty, Kirkwood Community College), State (Iowa DOT special projects grant), National Center for Mobility Management grant, passenger revenue
notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand or scheduled evening rides for workers/students; launched Dec 11, 2024; completed 4,200+ rides; pilot ended June 30, 2026 due to ~$350k/yr funding shortfall.

name: Mountain Rides Dial-a-Ride
area: Blaine County, ID: Ketchum, Sun Valley, Hailey, Bellevue
notes: Curb-to-curb paratransit available to qualifying individuals within the Mountain Rides service area; booked by phone (208-788-7433 x106). Agency otherwise runs fare-free fixed-route buses.

name: Pocatello Regional Transit Door-to-Door Services
area: Pocatello/Chubbuck urban area plus seven surrounding counties (Bannock, Bear Lake, Bingham, Caribou, Franklin, Oneida, Power) in Idaho Transportation District #5, southeast Idaho
operator: City of Pocatello / Pocatello Regional Transit (PRT)
booking: Phone (208-234-2287); NEMT trips booked via MTM (1-877-503-1261)
notes: Agency's Door-to-Door Services page states service is NOT open to the general public; eligibility limited to ADA-qualified riders unable to use fixed route, Medicaid/NEMT-eligible riders, seniors 60+ with health/functional limitations, and rural residents in outlying counties without fixed-route coverage. Reclassified from candidate's Demand-Response to Paratransit. Vendor, fares, hours, funding, launch year not confirmed from source.

name: SMART Transit Dial-A-Ride
area: Twin Falls and Jerome area (south-central Idaho)
operator: SMART Transit (South Central Community Action Partnership)
notes: General-public Dial-A-Ride demand-response; priority given to ADA riders and seniors 60+, then general public. Phone reservations only; same-day reservations not accepted (advance booking required). Shared-ride, ADA wheelchair accessible, fare-free.

name: Valley Regional Transit ACCESS Paratransit
area: Within 3/4 mile of VRT fixed-route service, Treasure Valley (Ada and Canyon counties / Boise metro), ID
fare: $3 per trip (certified passenger); PCA free; companion $3
hours: Mirrors VRT fixed-route service hours; reservations Mon-Fri 8am-5pm, Sat by voicemail
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for riders unable to use fixed-route/on-demand bus due to disability; trips booked up to 14 days ahead, no later than 5pm for next operating day. Operated by VRT via local municipal tax support. Related VRT specialized services (Beyond Access, City Go, Rides2Wellness, Volunteer Driver Program, VRT Late Night, VRT Lyft Pass) not individually verified here.

name: Access Johnson County Public Transit
area: Johnson County, IN (zone-to-zone countywide; Franklin, Greenwood, etc.)
notes: General-public demand-response ('Demand Response and Flexible Fixed Route service'); reservations by phone (317-738-5523) or the 'Trip Portal' smartphone app for registered riders; all vehicles wheelchair accessible; ADA paratransit certification available separately.

name: Access219 Paratransit
area: City of Gary plus 3/4 mile beyond fixed routes in Calumet Township, Crown Point, East Chicago, Griffith, Hammond, Highland, Hobart, Merrillville, and Munster (Lake County)
fare: $2.50 one-way within Gary; $4.00 one-way outside Gary; 20-ride local pass $50; 12-ride non-local pass $48
notes: ADA-complementary paratransit for riders unable to use GPTC fixed routes; three ADA eligibility categories (I/II/III).

name: BLink
area: Within Bloomington city limits (Downtown, East, and North zones); serves trips not within walkable distance of a fixed bus route
fare: $2 per one-way trip; pay in-app, cash (exact change), Tap To Pay, or Umo card
notes: No eligibility or application required; rides booked on demand or up to 24 hours in advance. Repeated no-shows/late cancellations may result in booking restrictions.

name: BT Access
area: City of Bloomington incorporated boundaries (Monroe County, IN)
hours: Mon-Fri 6:00am-11:59pm; Sat/Sun varies seasonally (7:30am-9:30pm during IU semesters)
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for persons with disabilities who cannot use fixed-route service; trips bookable up to 14 days in advance, same-day as capacity permits; reciprocal visitor eligibility up to 21 days.

name: Citilink Access
area: Fort Wayne (within 3/4 mile of fixed routes; Access Plus to Fort Wayne city limits)
fare: $3.00 (Access); $4.50 or $4.28 via Token Transit (Access Plus expanded zone)
hours: No service Sundays/holidays; reservation phone staffed 5:30 AM-8:30 PM weekdays, 7:30 AM-5:30 PM Saturdays
notes: Demand-response van service for riders with disabilities who meet ADA eligibility (application with 21-day determination) and are unable to use fixed-route service. Reservations recommended up to 14 days ahead, required by 5 PM prior day.

name: CityBus ACCESS
area: Greater Lafayette (Lafayette / West Lafayette, Tippecanoe County) ADA complementary service area
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for eligible individuals unable to use fixed-route buses; listed as a distinct service on the official CityBus site. CityBus also runs FLEX flexible-routing and CityVan services (excluded here). Ridership/performance figures not verified.

name: Hamilton County Express
area: Hamilton County, IN (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Westfield and contiguous counties)
hours: Mon-Fri 6:00am-6:00pm; Sat 7:00am-3:00pm; closed major holidays (booking line Mon-Fri 8am-4pm)
notes: General-public demand-response (reservation-based) transit in Hamilton County; open to individuals with disabilities and the general public; connects to contiguous counties. Booking via 317-773-2688.

name: IndyGo Access
area: Marion County, IN (ADA service area within 3/4 mile of fixed routes; extended coverage countywide)
operator: IndyGo (Indianapolis Public Transportation Corporation); operated under contract by MV Transportation
fare: $5.50 within 3/4 mile of fixed route; $11.00 beyond (countywide); $15.00 same-day Premium Service Area (effective July 1, 2026)
hours: Seven days a week, same hours as local fixed-route service
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for riders unable to use fixed-route service; same-day trips within Premium Service Area added July 1, 2026 based on vehicle/operator capacity.

name: METS Micro
area: City of Evansville, Indiana (designated on-demand zones; expanding to Jacobsville)
notes: Launched Nov 27, 2023; completed over 37,000 rides by first anniversary (Nov 2024). Powered by Via; supported by Toyota Mobility Foundation, Evansville MPO, and Energy Systems Network. Curb-to-curb; booking by app or phone (812-562-5011). Expanding to Jacobsville.

name: MITSPlus
area: Muncie, IN (ADA complementary paratransit service area)
hours: Mon-Fri 6:15 AM-6:45 PM; Sat 8:15 AM-6:15 PM; Sun closed
notes: Origin-to-destination van service for persons with disabilities unable to use MITS fixed-route bus; eligibility requires two-part application with professional assessment (ADA complementary paratransit).

name: Transpo Access
area: South Bend / Mishawaka; within 3/4 mile of Transpo fixed-route service area
fare: $2.00 per trip leg (twice fixed-route fare, per ADA)
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for riders with disabilities certified under DOT eligibility criteria; service limited to within 3/4 mile of fixed routes.

name: Lawrence Transit On Demand
area: City limits of Lawrence, Douglas County, KS (curb-to-curb, citywide zone)
operator: Lawrence Transit (City of Lawrence / University of Kansas partnership)
fare: $3 one-way (credit/debit only, no cash), effective March 1, 2026
hours: Daytime: 8 a.m.–6 p.m. Sunday; Nighttime: 8 p.m.–6 a.m. Mon–Sat and 12 a.m.–6 a.m. Sunday
fleet: Smaller buses, all ADA accessible and equipped with bike racks (count not specified)
notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand shared-ride service open to the general public, book any two points in town; booked via Lawrence Transit On Demand app (Spare, iOS/Android) or phone (785) 312-7054. Ridership/performance data not published on site.

name: Night Line
area: Within Lawrence city limits, Douglas County, KS
fare: $2 cash only per trip (passes not accepted)
notes: Evening/overnight curb-to-curb on-demand service open to the general public; rides scheduled by phone in advance during business hours (8 a.m.–5 p.m.) rather than fixed-stop. Originally launched as a one-year pilot on June 1, 2013; still listed as a core Lawrence Transit service.

name: RideKC Freedom On-Demand (Kansas portion)
area: Johnson County and Wyandotte County, Kansas (part of the RideKC Kansas City metro service area)
operator: Kansas City Area Transportation Authority (RideKC / KCATA)
fare: $5.00 for the first 5 miles, $2.00 per mile after that
notes: Same-day curb-to-curb on-demand mobility service for RideKC Freedom (paratransit) eligible riders; unlike traditional paratransit, no day-ahead scheduling is required for eligible trips. Kansas-side coverage includes all of Johnson County and Wyandotte County; also serves Kansas City and Independence, Missouri.

name: The Lift (Topeka Metro Paratransit)
area: City of Topeka, Shawnee County, KS (ADA service area matching fixed-route coverage)
hours: Same days/times as fixed route (Mon-Fri 5:35am-6:40pm; Sat 8:15am-6:40pm)
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for qualified passengers unable to use Topeka Metro fixed-route service; operates same days/times as fixed route. Reservations via (785) 783-7000.

name: Wichita Transit Paratransit
area: City of Wichita, Sedgwick County (ADA service area, incl. within 3/4 mile of fixed routes)
notes: ADA complementary paratransit for persons with physical, cognitive, or visual disabilities functionally unable to use fixed-route buses; eligibility via application, interview, and functional assessment. Trips scheduled day-before, up to 7 days in advance; same-day subject to availability. Extended evening service within 3/4 mile of fixed routes.
